text:
alex: Quick question — how should routing policy behave across free/pro/enterprise when the preferred model variant is out or overloaded? do we silently fallback to a quantized variant, apply a soft cap, or return 429/503? Need consistent console UX and telemetry.

mira: My vote: graceful fallback for free/pro with a soft-cap and penalty; enterprise should default to deny fallback unless tenant opts in. we should make it explicit in the API and console. :+1:

jordan: Agreed. We also need a clear API contract for `fallback_policy`. something like allow|deny|notify and a penalty weight. small config sketch below.

jordan: ```json
{
  "fallback": "allow",
  "penalty": 0.2,
  "soft_cap_tokens": 1000000,
  "grace_window_s": 300
}
```

alex: That looks good. Key UX things: show in route preview what will happen on primary miss, show cost delta, and surface a per-tenant boolean `notify_on_fallback`.

paul: Telemetry concerns — we need metrics: `fallback_count`, `fallback_rate`, `quality_regressions`, `token_cost_saved`, and `latency_p95_by_variant`. Without those we risk silent regressions. also need to tie fallback events to prompt sets for evals.

liz: Console UX idea: small badge on the model-route card — "fallback allowed" with a tooltip showing penalty and expected cost delta. preview should simulate N requests and show fraction that would fallback. :bulb:

mira: Edge cases: if primary becomes available mid-request we must be deterministic — pick a variant at decision time and stick with it for the whole request. for batching: prefer keeping batch homogenous to avoid cache fragmentation (KV cache).

jordan: API signal handling: free/pro maybe degrade silently for best UX; enterprise should get explicit error code when fallback is disallowed. propose header `X-Redwood-Fallback: variant=quant-8` when fallback happens and structured body with reason. also return `Retry-After` when we're failing due to capacity.

alex: We should avoid silent quality regressions — add `fallback_score` (0..1) to telemetry for each request and a `notify_on_fallback` flag to enable tenant alerts. default for pro/free: notify_on_fallback=false, enterprise=true.

ops-bot: incident-bot: alert created: fallback_rate>5% && error_rate>1% for 5m -> paging rule engaged.

paul: Implementation note: router decision = tenant_policy + tier_defaults + regional_capacity + runtime_penalty. pseudocode:

paul: ```
if (primary.available && within_quota) use(primary)
else if (fallback_allowed && fallback_score >= tenant.threshold) use(fallback)
else if (tenant.is_enterprise && !fallback_allowed) fail_with(503, "fallback_not_allowed")
else fail_with(429, "quota_exceeded")
```

alex: Proposed tier defaults (to iterate on):
- free: fallback=allow, penalty=0.0, monthly_softcap_tokens=5_000_000, grace_window=300s
- pro: fallback=allow, penalty=0.1, monthly_softcap_tokens=50_000_000, grace_window=180s
- enterprise: fallback=deny (default), admin_toggle=true, grace_window=0s

mira: I'll add telemetry metrics and a dashboard tile: `Fallback by tier`, `Avg cost delta`, `Quality regressions` and a heatmap by region. this will help tune penalty and thresholds. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jordan: I'll draft the API contract and error code semantics. also need migration plan so existing tenants get sane defaults and we don't change behavior silently.

alex: Can @mira and @jordan pair and drop a short RFC in eng-platform RFCs by EOD tomorrow? then we can follow with a small console PR for preview and a router PR for decision logic. :thumbsup:

liz: fwiw — small thing: include a per-route simulated "monthly cost delta" estimate in console so sales can show customers impact before toggling fallback.

alex: Great, thanks everyone. we'll iterate on defaults in the RFC and wire up telem first so we can measure.
